steps: Sign in and stay on the Chat screen with the left sidebar.
Click "New chat" in the sidebar (the same control is in the collapsed rail).
Look for an empty conversation with the message box ready to type in, then type a message and send it.
Compare with Expected: a new empty chat with a ready composer.

S4.02.needs: a past conversation in the sidebar
steps: Sign in and look at the sidebar list under the "Recents" heading.
Click a past conversation title.
Look for its earlier messages (transcript) and a message box to continue the chat.
Compare with Expected: transcript shown and the chat can be continued.

S4.03.needs: a past conversation with a known word in it
S4.03.note: The code does not show whether results update while typing or only after Enter; the tester should try both. Command key plus K opens "Search Conversations" in the command palette as a second route.
steps: Click "Search" in the sidebar.
In the box "Search your workspace", type a word from a past chat title or message.
Wait for matching past conversations to appear.
Click one result and check that its conversation opens.

S4.04.needs: at least one archived chat (archive one from its row menu first)
S4.04.note: The sidebar button appears only when at least one chat is archived. Delete moves a chat to "Recently deleted" and does not remove it at once.
steps: Open the account menu and choose "Settings", then "Privacy".
Find "Archived chats" and click "Manage".
Check the list of archived chats; try "Restore" on one and check it returns to the sidebar.
Try the sidebar "Archived (N)" button as a second route and compare with Expected: open, restore or delete.
Open the menu of a chat row in the sidebar and click "Pin".
Look for the "Pinned" section at the top of the chat list.
Click the pinned chat and check that it opens.
Open its menu again and click "Unpin"; check that it leaves the Pinned section.
S4.05.where: Sidebar > Pinned section, set from a chat row's menu > Pin

steps: Click "Projects" in the left rail.
Look for the list of your projects.
Click "New project" and check that a create dialog opens.
Click an existing project card and check that it opens.

S4.07.note: The project home is a page with tabs; a description summary was not confirmed in the files read.
steps: Click "Projects" in the left rail and open a project card.
Check the project name heading at the top.
Check the tabs "Chats", "Artifacts", "Work", "Sources", "Scheduled".
Compare with Expected: name, description or instructions, and entries to its chats and files.

S4.08.needs: a project with at least one chat in it
steps: Open a project.
Click the "Chats" tab.
Check the list of this project's conversations.
Click one and check that it opens.

S4.09.note: Project settings also has a "Files" section with a knowledge files panel. The remove control was not confirmed in the files read. Google Drive needs its connector.
steps: Open a project and click the "Sources" tab.
Click "Add sources" and choose a file, Google Drive, or "Add text".
Check that the new item appears in the Sources list.
Look for a remove control on that item and check that it removes it.
S4.09.where: Projects > a project > Sources tab > Add sources

S4.10.note: Whether the instructions change the reply is not checked by this code read.
steps: Open a project and click "Project options".
Click "Project settings".
Type text in the "Instructions" box and click "Save".
Open a new chat in that project and check that the reply follows the instructions.
S4.10.where: Projects > a project > Project options > Project settings > Instructions

S4.11.needs: a second account in the same workspace
S4.11.note: The owner is listed with the label "Owner". Only the owner can add or remove people, per Expected; not tested here.
steps: Open a project, click "Project options", then "Share".
Click "Add people" and pick a person from the workspace.
Choose "Can view" or "Can edit" for that person.
Check that the person appears in the member list; then check it from the second account.
S4.11.where: Projects > a project > Project options > Share

labels.text: Use memories from outside this project

steps: Open a project's "Project settings".
Scroll to the "Memory" section and read the "Project memories" list.
Add a memory in the box "Add a memory only this project uses".
Check it appears only in this project and that the "Use memories from outside this project" checkbox is shown separately from account memory.
S4.12.where: Projects > a project > Project options > Project settings > Memory

S4.13.needs: a paid account (the code hides Work on a free trial)
S4.13.note: The mode button is shown only when the plan allows AGI Work.
steps: On the new chat screen, open the mode control in the message box and choose "Work".
Type a goal for an autonomous task and send it.
Check that the screen shows the work run and that "Work history" is reachable from the command palette or the home screen.
Compare with Expected: a place to state a goal and reach recent work.

S4.14.note: The home link appears only above a set number of runs.
steps: Press Command plus K and choose "Work history", or go to the home screen and click "Work history" if it appears.
Click the filter "Active".
Check that running work tasks show their live status.
Click "All" and check that finished tasks also appear.
S4.14.where: Work history (command palette "Work history", or the "Work history" link on the home screen when there are many runs)

S4.15.note: The outputs section was not confirmed in the detail panel file read.
steps: Open "Work history" and click a task.
Check the "Task details" panel for the status, the "Task goal" and the "Task plan".
Look for any pending decision or approval on the panel.
Compare with Expected: status, step-by-step activity, outputs and pending decision.

S4.16.needs: a work task that is waiting for approval
S4.16.note: There is no separate approvals inbox; pending approvals are gathered under the "Needs you" filter.
steps: Open "Work history" and click the filter "Needs you".
Check the tasks waiting for a decision and their approval cards.
Click the approve or deny button on one card.
Check that the card updates to show the decision.

S4.17.note: Status filters include Active, Paused, Completed, Failed and Expired.
steps: Click "Scheduled" in the sidebar.
Click "Create a task" (or "New task") and fill in and save a schedule.
On a schedule card, use the menu item "Run now", then "Pause" or "Resume".
Click the edit control ("Edit Schedule") and the "Delete" menu item, and compare with Expected.

S4.18.needs: a schedule that has run at least once
S4.18.note: There is no separate routine page; the configuration is seen on the card and in the edit dialog. Next run display was not confirmed in the files read.
steps: Click "Scheduled" in the sidebar.
On a schedule card click the "Run History" button to expand its run history.
Click "Edit Schedule" to see the prompt and cadence.
Compare with Expected: prompt, cadence, next run and run history.
S4.18.where: Sidebar > Scheduled > a schedule card > Run History

S4.19.note: The page says Code is on paid plans.
steps: Click "Code" in the sidebar switch.
Look for the "Cloud sessions" list.
Click "New" and choose a repository with "Select repository".
Click "Start the task" and check that a new session starts.

S4.20.needs: a Code session that has run
S4.20.note: The message box label used for steering a running session was not confirmed in the files read.
steps: Click "Code" in the sidebar switch and open a session in the "Cloud sessions" list.
Check the session transcript.
Click "Changes" to see the file changes and the diff.
Look for a message box to send the next instruction and compare with Expected.
S4.20.where: Sidebar > Code > Cloud sessions > a session

S4.21.note: No pairing control was found in this web panel, although Expected lists pair.
steps: Open the account menu, choose "Settings", then "Account".
Scroll to "Linked devices" and read each device's status.
Click "Rename", type a new name, click "Save", and check the new name.
Click "Unlink" and confirm "Unlink device"; check that the device leaves the list.
Click "Library" in the sidebar.
Look at the filter tabs "All", "Images", "Videos", "Documents", "Artifacts", "Uploads", "Generated files".
Choose a file and open its menu or "Download" action.
Compare with Expected: files, images, videos, documents and artifacts, with filters and open or download.

S4.24.needs: a second account in the same workspace
S4.24.note: Found only the workspace console page "Sharing" (apps/web/features/workspace-console/components/WorkspaceConsoleNav.tsx), which lists what the workspace shares, not what others share with the user. Shared projects show the label "Shared with you" on the project page (apps/web/app/chat/projects/[id]/page.tsx). No list of items shared with the user was found.

S4.25.note: The old address /chat/artifacts redirects to the Library Artifacts filter.
steps: Click "Library" in the sidebar.
Click the filter "Artifacts".
Click one artifact to open it.
Compare with Expected: a gallery of generated artifacts that opens any one of them.

S4.26.needs: a chat with a text document artifact
S4.26.note: "Edit source" appears only for some artifacts and not while a preview is shown.
steps: Open a chat that produced a text document artifact and open it in the side panel.
Open the more menu and click "Edit source".
Change the text, then click "Save" (tooltip "Save as a new version").
Open the version history and check that a new version exists with the change.
S4.26.where: A chat > artifact side panel > more menu (...) > Edit source

S4.27.needs: a signed-in account; image generation may depend on plan (not verified)
S4.27.note: No dedicated image studio found: searched apps/web and packages/ui for 'image studio' and the image routes; apps/web/app/chat/images/page.tsx redirects to /chat/library?tab=images. The + button's own label was not found.
steps: Click Chat in the left rail to open a new chat.
Click the + button in the composer and choose Generate image.
Look for the Image chip in the composer, then open the aspect ratio control (Select aspect ratio) and the Add a style to the prompt control.

Type a description and send. Compare with Expected: the picture should appear in the chat. There is no studio page with prompt, style, size and history in one place; /chat/images only redirects to Library > Images.
S4.27.where: Chat > the + button in the composer > Generate image (no separate studio page)

S4.28.needs: a few generated or uploaded images in the account
S4.28.note: Remix appears only when the host provides remixItem (LibraryView.tsx:701 and :294); the row-menu text was not located as a literal.
steps: Click Library in the left rail.
Click the Images tab.
Hover an image and look for its download control and any Remix action in its row menu (Remix shows only where the host supports it).
Check that generated and uploaded images both appear here, and compare with Expected: open, download and remix actions.

S4.30.needs: at least one image or video generation job in the account
S4.30.note: Whether a job links to its result was not confirmed in the code read.
steps: Click Library in the left rail.
Look for the Generations heading above the tabs.
Check the status words on each job: Queued, Generating, Failed, Done, Cancelled.
Open a finished job and see whether it links to its result, then compare with Expected.

S4.31.needs: a project; a file to upload (optional)
S4.31.note: Studio tiles start a chat that makes the output; no separate reader or annotation view was found for sources.
steps: Click Projects in the left rail and open a project.
Click the Sources tab.
Click Add sources, add a text note or a file, and check it is listed.
Look at the Studio tiles (Briefing doc, Study guide and others) and compare with Expected: the sources are the notebook, and the outputs appear from them.

S4.32.needs: a conversation that has run Deep Research
S4.32.note: The Library tab renders ResearchReportsGallery with a Load older reports control; the panel opens from the chat toolbar, not the rail.
steps: Open a conversation that ran Deep Research.
Hover the sources button; its title is Research sources, and click it to open the panel.
Click the Library tab, then open a report.
Check the report's sections (Report tab) and cited sources, and compare with Expected.
S4.32.where: Chat > a conversation with research sources > Open sources panel (title Research sources) > Library tab

S4.35.needs: a signed-in account; skills may be limited by plan
S4.35.note: Install, enable, disable and remove controls for skills were not found as literal labels; the account menu trigger was not traced.
steps: Open the account menu and click Settings.
Under Customize, click Skills.
Click New skill, fill in the editor, and click Create skill.
Check the list for installed and available skills and their controls, then compare with Expected.

S4.36.note: Configure and Update controls were not found as literal labels.
steps: Open the account menu, click Settings, then Customize > Plugins.
Compare the installed and available plugin lists.
Click Install on an available plugin.
Open a plugin's remove action and look for the Remove plugin? confirmation, then compare with Expected.

S4.37.needs: an outside account for the service to connect
S4.37.note: Labels come from the shared SettingsModal; the web adapter path was not run.
steps: Open the account menu, click Settings, then Connectors under Customize.
Look at the Connected tab and the list of services.
Click Connect on one service, then Reconnect or Disconnect on a connected one (Disconnect asks to confirm).
Compare with Expected: the list should update to the new state.

S4.38.note: The composer model control's own label was not located; find it by the current model name.
steps: Open a new chat and open the model control in the composer.
Look for the Models panel with Search models, Context ceiling and Capabilities for each model.
Pick a model, then open Settings > General.
Under Preferences, check the Default model row, choose a model, and compare with Expected.
S4.38.where: Composer model picker (Models panel) and Settings > General > Preferences > Default model

S4.39.needs: a signed-in account with some usage
S4.39.note: Plan usage limits heading shows an upgrade title on Free plans instead.
steps: Open the account menu, click Settings, then Usage.
Read Plan usage limits and Credit balances, and check the Resets section.
Scroll to Monthly spend limit and check its figure.
Scroll to Where your usage went, switch between By day, By week and By month, and compare with Expected.

S4.40.needs: a paid account for the plan and invoice views (test checkout per the product note)
S4.40.note: No separate cancel control was found; cancelling appears to go through Manage billing. The plan says this path is unfinished.
steps: Open the account menu, click Settings, then Billing.
Check the plan name, Renews on date and the Payment section.
Check the Invoices table, then click Adjust plan (or Upgrade plan on Free) and look at the options.
Click Manage billing and compare with Expected (in Electron it opens outside the app).

S4.41.note: No Save control label was checked; appearance, personalization and notifications are separate panes.
steps: Open the account menu, click Settings, then General.
Under Profile, change Full name.
Scroll to Preferences and change Default model or Display Language.
Leave the screen, come back, and check the change was kept, then compare with Expected.

S4.42.needs: an admin or owner account; a second account to invite
S4.42.note: Non-admin users may see a different view; not checked.
steps: Open the account menu, click Settings, then Workspace.
Follow the link to the workspace console and look at Overview, Members, Roles, Identity and Policy.
On Members or Roles, check invitations and seats, and invite a second account.
Compare with Expected: an admin can manage members, roles, invitations and policy.
S4.42.where: Account menu > Settings > Workspace (then the workspace console: Members, Roles, Policy)

S4.43.note: The page exists at /developers (apps/web/app/developers/page.tsx, heading Developer console in apps/web/features/developers/components/DeveloperConsolePage.tsx) with API keys (apps/web/features/settings/components/Settings/ApiKeys.tsx). Searched for links to /developers and the navDeveloperConsole string in the signed-in nav, Settings and Account menu: none found, so no UI path was confirmed.

S4.44.note: The account menu trigger was not traced; the Send feedback dialog's own opener was not traced beyond the menu item.
steps: Open the account menu and hover Get help.
Click Send feedback and choose a feedback type in the dialog, then send.
Open Settings > Help and check the links: Documentation, Help center, Contact support, Report a bug, Release notes, System status, Legal.
Compare with Expected: help links and a feedback path should both be there.
S4.44.where: Account menu > Get help > Send feedback; Settings > Help
